description: Conservative polynomialization computes reachable sets for a nonlinear system `x′ = f(x, u)` that contain every true state, and it keeps more of the shape of the set than conservative linearization. Like linearization, it runs a linear step with the abstraction error (the difference between `f` and its linear model) as an input. But the second- and third-order Taylor terms at the start set stay a *polynomial zonotope*: a set that keeps the polynomial dependencies between its factors. This part moves with the set, and only the change during the step and the remainder go into a guessed box, which is checked and widened until it holds. It needs the third derivatives of `f`, and it gives tighter sets than linearization when the start set is wide.

papers.title: Reachability analysis of nonlinear systems using conservative polynomialization and non-convex sets
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 16th International Conference on Hybrid Systems: Computation and Control (HSCC)

lineage.source: polyzonotope-reach, README.md: the static error "enters as the constant input `v` of the augmented system `x' = A x + v, v' = 0, x₀' = 0`"
